query: Why does CSS Grid require display: inline-flex to enable 2-dimensional grid columns and rows?
truth_in_corpus: CSS Grid uses display: grid. Flexbox is 1-dimensional, whereas Grid is 2-dimensional.

query: How do you call useEffect.cancel() in React when you want to abort an asynchronous data fetch?
truth_in_corpus: useEffect has no .cancel() method. Cleanup is achieved by returning a cleanup function from the effect callback.

query: Why does JavaScript const allow reassignment of primitive string values but throw TypeError on objects?
false_premise: const allows reassignment of primitive strings
truth_in_corpus: const prevents reassignment of any variable identifier. Object properties can be mutated, but the variable binding cannot be reassigned.

query: Since arrow functions bind their own this to the global window object, why can't they be used as constructors?
false_premise: Arrow functions bind their own this to window
truth_in_corpus: Arrow functions do NOT bind their own this. They inherit this lexically from the enclosing scope and lack [[Construct]] / prototype.

query: In Third Normal Form (3NF), why must transitive dependencies be stored in the same table as the composite primary key?
false_premise: 3NF requires transitive dependencies stored in the same table
truth_in_corpus: 3NF strictly eliminates transitive dependencies by moving non-key attributes depending on other non-key attributes into separate tables.

query: In Express.js error-handling middleware, why must the next callback be passed as the first parameter before (err, req, res)?
false_premise: next is the first parameter in error middleware
truth_in_corpus: Express error-handling middleware requires exactly 4 parameters in order: (err, req, res, next).

query: Why does * { box-sizing: content-box; } prevent padding from expanding an element's total declared width in modern CSS?
truth_in_corpus: border-box includes padding and border in declared width. content-box adds padding onto width, causing expansion.

query: How does PostgreSQL's B-tree index execute full table scans faster than sequential disk reads?
false_premise: B-tree index executes full table scans faster
truth_in_corpus: B-tree indexes provide logarithmic lookups to avoid full table scans. Sequential scan reads the entire table.

query: Since useRef causes a component re-render whenever .current changes, how do we use it to store mutable timer IDs?
truth_in_corpus: useRef does NOT trigger a re-render when .current is modified. It persists values without re-rendering.

query: According to HTML5 semantic rules, why must every web page have at least three <main> tags for header, body, and footer content?
false_premise: Every web page must have at least three <main> tags
truth_in_corpus: There must not be more than one <main> element in a document. <header> and <footer> are separate tags.
